summary: Peter Lindegger-Stauffer was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He received an honorary Ph.D. from the University of Fribourg in 1998 and served as curator at the Tibet Institute Rikon from 1967 to 1974.

Peter M. Scharf, an Indologist and linguist, earned his Ph.D. under George Cardona at the University of Pennsylvania. In 2002 he founded the Sanskrit Library and later held posts at Brown University, IIIT Hyderabad, and IIAS.
Peter Masefield worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under L. P. N. Perera and completed his doctoral work under Ninian Smart.

Peter Moran specialized in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Tufts University and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Washington under Charles Keyes, also studying under teachers including Leonard van der Kuijp and Geshe Nawang Lhundrup Nornang.

Peter N. Gregory is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as Executive Director and editor for the Kuroda Institute and taught at UIUC and Smith College.

Peter Nicolas Harting studied at Utrecht University under Willem Caland, earning an M.A. and Ph.D. A scholar of linguistics and Indology, he taught Dutch in London and Oxford before becoming Professor of English at Groningen and Amsterdam.

Peter Percival was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Principal of Jaffna Central College (1832–1851), taught at St Augustine's College, and became Registrar at the University of Madras and Professor at Presidency University in 1856.

Peter Peterson studied at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford, under Theodor Aufrecht, Monier Monier-Williams, and Max Müller. An Indologist, he served as Sanskrit Professor at Elphinstone College and Registrar at the University of Mumbai.

Peter Schreiner studied at Temple, Münster (Promotion under Paul Hacker), and Tübingen (Habilitation). A scholar of Indology and religious studies, he held posts at Tübingen, lectured at SOAS in 1988, and became a professor at Zurich in 1990.
Peter Schwabland is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his M.A. at the University of Washington in 1994 under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.

Peter Schwieger, a scholar of Tibetology, studied under Dieter Schuh and completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Bonn. He held a visiting professorship at Humboldt University and assumed the Tibetology chair at Bonn in 2001.

Peter Scott Noble was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Aberdeen and Cambridge under E. J. Rapson and Peter Giles. He held professorships of Latin and Humanity before serving as Principal of King's College London and Vice-Chancellor of London University.

Peter Skilling studied under Heinz Bechert and Cristina Scherrer-Schaub, earning his PhD from the EPHE. Active in Buddhist studies and Indology, he founded the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation and taught at Chulalongkorn University and the EFEO.

Peter Stewart studied at Clare College, Cambridge, and works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held positions at Reading, the Ure Museum, and the Courtauld Institute before joining Oxford in 2011 as Associate Professor and head of the CARC.

Peter Stumpf was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt from 1959 to 1968, completing his Ph.D. under Werner Thomas, and worked there as an assistant until 1977.
Peter Thomi is an Indologist who studied under Alfred Bloch. He served as the head of the Institut für Indologie Wichtrach, attested in 1995.

Peter Zieme, a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, studied at Humboldt University. He worked at the GDR Academy of Sciences and Berlin-Brandenburg Academy, later serving as honorary professor at the Free University of Berlin.

Peter van der Veer studied at Groningen and Utrecht. Specializing in religious studies, Indology, and sinology, he held professorships at Amsterdam, Utrecht, and Göttingen, and served as Director of the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

Peter von Bohlen studied at Halle, Bonn, and Berlin under Wilhelm Gesenius, A. W. von Schlegel, Georg Freytag, and Franz Bopp. An Indologist, he became ordinary professor of oriental literature at the University of Königsberg in 1828.

Peter von Bradke studied at Tartu, Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, Jena (Ph.D.), Munich, Leipzig, and Giessen. An Indologist and linguist, he became Privatdozent in 1884 and extraordinary professor in 1886 at the University of Giessen.
